summary: New deployment path: an official router container image (ADR-0116, proposed in #177; ADR-0121 proposed here) plus a compose example, a CI build-and-start job and a static self-test. Router code changes only VERSION (0.38.0); no route, auth, enrollment, data-class, cloud or session logic changes. Supply chain (TM-16, B9): base image python:3.14-slim-trixie pinned by index digest (checked by check_pinned_references, updated by Dependabot); every Python package from the new router/requirements-container-lock.txt with all PyPI hashes, installed with --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all: (no sdist build scripts, no resolution), versions equal to the CI lock; verified in the build (pydeps verify, pip check, imports) and pip removed afterwards; lock_requirements check/verify-pypi and pip-audit now cover the lock. Host impact (TM-14, B8): the router runs as uid/gid 10001 with no capabilities (CapEff 0 verified), compose adds read-only root, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL; /etc/skirnir-router is mounted read-only and the program folder is root-owned, both verified unwritable from the running container; only the state and log volumes are writable. No secret is baked in (no ENV/ARG secret names, no COPY of configuration or certificates, .dockerignore excludes config/ and *.env); secrets arrive via env_file. Posture/ProcessView (TM-14): in the container a read-only certificate mount is a read-only mount, so tls_files_changeable is not raised; the start reported only control_on_network (info), so no posture code change was needed. Logs (TM-15): router log to stdout as before; entrypoint sets umask 077 like UMask=0077 (state files observed 0600). The health probe sends GET /api/version (auth-exempt) over loopback without certificate verification and carries no secret. --init runs as root only in a one-off container with the config folder writable, equivalent to sudo router.py --init on a host, and hands config.yaml to root:10001 0640 like setup_init.readable_for_router. The compose PostgreSQL service is not published to the host and gets its password from its own env file; locally built images use pull_policy: never so a same-named registry image is never pulled. CI job container builds and runs PR code with Docker on the runner without secrets (persist-credentials false) and pushes nothing. Refreshed after merging origin/main with the whole first portability wave (router 0.37.2, agent 0.36.0, ADRs 0101-0120, including install.sh --without-mqtt and pydeps --without): no router requirement changed, so the container lock stays as pinned; the image's pydeps.py verify call is unaffected (--without is optional); install.sh's program-file list is still covered by the image (selftest_container_image parity check). Conflicts were only VERSION, CHANGELOG, the ADR index and this record; the changed paths are the same 23 as reviewed. Checks re-run on the merged tree.

findings.evidence: router/compose.yaml publishes 11434 and 11435 on all host addresses (as the systemd unit listens on 0.0.0.0). Docker forwards published ports with its own packet-filter rules before ufw's or firewalld's usual INPUT rules, so an operator following the existing Firewall section could leave the control port reachable from everywhere (TM-03 exposure of the admin UI and tunnel; login and TLS still apply).
findings.resolution: docs/install-router.md and .de.md (Container) say so and name the remedies: the DOCKER-USER chain, publishing on one host address, or 127.0.0.1 behind a reverse proxy. The default stays all addresses because remote agents must reach 11435; control_auth and TLS remain the controls.

findings.evidence: The first draft added router/requirements-container-lock.txt without adding it to the pip-audit of hash-locked sets in .github/workflows/security.yml, so a vulnerable pinned version in the image would not have been reported (TM-16).
findings.resolution: security.yml audits it with pip-audit --require-hashes --disable-pip; lock_requirements.py verify-pypi and check include it. Local run: No known vulnerabilities found.

findings.evidence: compose.yaml refers to the locally built image by the short name skirnir-router; without a pull policy, compose (or Podman short-name resolution) would try a registry when the local image is missing and could run an unrelated image of that name (TM-16).
findings.resolution: pull_policy: never on the router and the locally built embed service; test/selftest_container_image.py asserts it for the router.

limitations: The image's Debian base packages are not scanned (no container image scanner in CI); pip-audit covers only the Python lock. Base updates arrive as Dependabot digest PRs.
Publishing to a registry, an image SBOM and build provenance (ADR-0116) are not implemented: CI builds and tests only; publishing is the maintainer's release decision.

compose.yaml was validated with docker-compose config (default, sessions and decision profiles); a full compose up was not run. The smoke test starts the container with the same flags as compose.yaml. The sessions and decision services were not started.

Secrets passed as environment variables are visible to anyone who can inspect the container (docker group, root-equivalent), comparable to secrets.env readable by root and the router's group on a host.
The --init one-off container runs as root with the engine's default capabilities and a writable bind mount, by design (like sudo router.py --init).
The CI container job runs PR code in Docker on the runner without secrets, as the existing jobs run PR Python; the ci.yml and security.yml changes need explicit maintainer review.
Locally the smoke script's published-port check cannot connect inside the WSL-based Podman machine, so its last line is STATE: failed there; the CI Docker job is the authoritative run.
